claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response with rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability is governed by nanoscale compositional heterogeneities.
Grain-boundary compositional heterogeneities enhance localized magnetostructural coupling near the operating temperature.
The initial alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure on the microscale.
The controlled annealing treatment will induce mild nanoscale phase separation.
The controlled annealing treatment will modify grain boundaries.
The intervention will produce nanoscale compositional variations.
The intervention will increase the density of modified grain boundaries.
Nanoscale heterogeneities create regions with altered magnetic anisotropy.
Nanoscale heterogeneities create regions with altered local exchange interactions.
Altered magnetic anisotropy and local exchange interactions facilitate spin reorientation under low magnetic fields.
Easier low-field spin reorientation enhances the magnetocaloric effect.
Modified grain boundaries promote rapid phonon-mediated heat exchange.
The modified grain boundaries do not introduce significant magnetic hysteresis.
The modified grain boundaries do not cause mechanical softening.
The annealed alloy will have a higher low-field isothermal magnetic entropy change than the homogeneous baseline.
The annealed alloy will have a greater low-field adiabatic temperature change than the homogeneous baseline.
The annealed alloy will have lower magnetic hysteresis than the homogeneous baseline.
The annealed alloy will maintain or improve mechanical stability relative to the homogeneous baseline.
The hypothesis applies near room temperature at applied magnetic fields below approximately 1 T for alloys of similar composition and processing history.
The predicted effects arise from nanoscale modifications rather than bulk phase changes.
